items.stem: Which statement about Kusto Query Language (KQL) is true?

options.text: It is a read-only language that processes data and returns results
options.rationale: Correct: KQL is a read-only request that returns results.

options.text: It modifies rows in place in the source table
options.rationale: Incorrect: KQL does not modify the underlying data.
Incorrect: KQL aggregates with summarize and related operators.

items.explanation: Correct: KQL is a read-only request that returns results.

items.stem: Which TWO are recommended KQL best practices? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Select the table with the fewest rows first in a join
options.rationale: Correct: placing the smaller table first improves join performance.

options.text: Use limit or count at the end of new queries
options.rationale: Correct: this avoids returning unexpectedly large result sets.

options.text: Convert billions of records before filtering
options.rationale: Incorrect: reduce data before conversion to avoid heavy processing.

options.text: Always use tolower() for case-insensitive comparisons
options.rationale: Incorrect: prefer the =~ operator over tolower() for comparisons.

items.explanation: Correct: placing the smaller table first improves join performance.

items.stem: Which KQL operator merges the rows of two tables by matching values of specified columns?

options.rationale: Correct: join merges rows of two tables on matching column values.
summarize aggregates one table; it does not merge two.
project selects columns within one table.
where filters rows within one table.

items.explanation: Correct: join merges rows of two tables on matching column values.
